heroHeadline: CSIS REPORT FINDS EUROPEAN NATO SPENDING UP 50% SINCE 2022, PUSHES BACK ON 'BURDEN-SHIFTING' (SEP 8); RUTTE DECLARES 'NATO 3.0' ALLIANCE'S BIGGEST SHIFT SINCE COLD WAR IN BERLIN (SEP 10); PISTORIUS-HEGSETH RECONCILIATION MEETING AND SEP 18 COLBY-EUCOM TROOP-OPTIONS BRIEFING STILL PENDING
heroSubtitle: As of September 13, 2026, the NATO-US tensions story remained centered on burden-sharing for Ukraine and the broader 'NATO 3.0' framework for shifting conventional-defense responsibility to Europe, with no major new US-NATO friction reported this week. At the 36th Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting on September 8, Pentagon Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby told the roughly 50-nation coalition that Washington 'cannot predict' when the war ends and that European partners must fund and arm Ukraine's defense, pointing to the PURL scheme as the ongoing US contribution model; partners pledged fresh UK, Dutch and Norwegian funding and roughly 1,000 additional Patriot interceptors even as Ukraine flagged an €8 billion gap. The same day, a CSIS analysis by Jerry McGinn and Celia Barrie found European NATO members and Canada have raised defense spending more than 50% since 2022 — Poland +71%, the Baltic states +134%, Scandinavia +126% — and tallied over $50 billion in new US-allied defense-industrial agreements since the Ankara summit, arguing deeper industrial cooperation, not a US drawdown, should be the goal even as the US still accounts for roughly 70% of total NATO spending. Two days later, on September 10, NATO Secretary General Rutte used Germany's Heads of Mission Conference in Berlin to call 'NATO 3.0' 'the most profound transformation of the Alliance since the Cold War,' citing Germany's new Lithuania brigade and eastern-flank corps command as proof points. Neither development addressed the Pentagon's Europe force-posture review directly; German Defense Minister Pistorius' planned September 15 Washington meeting with US Defense Secretary Hegseth — their first since an earlier snub — and the September 18 Colby-EUCOM decision briefing remain the next concrete checkpoints.
